question:
A 19-year-old woman with an unremarkable medical history seeks medical attention for recent onset of
neck and left upper limb pain. She describes experiencing intermittent numbness and weakness in her
left arm and hand. The symptoms began as a tingling sensation that has progressively worsened over
the past month. She rates both neck and upper extremity pain as 5/10, with increased intensity during
limb movement. Physical examination reveals hypertonic bilateral trapezius muscles and cool left
fingertips. When the patient assumes a position with her chest thrust forward, and her left shoulder is
extended and depressed with downward traction, there is a decrease in radial pulse accompanied by
extremity pain. Which test is demonstrated to be positive in this clinical scenario? Answer Choices: (A)
Adson’s test (B) Roos test (C) EAST test (D) Spurling's test (E) Wright's hyperabduction test (F) Military
posture test (G) Costoclavicular test (H) Allen's test (I) Phalen’s test (J) Tinel's sign
 A. Military posture test
B. Wright's hyperabduction test
C. Tinel's sign
D. Costoclavicular test
E. Roos test
F. EAST test
G. Spurling's test
H. Allen's test
I. Phalen’s test
J. Adson’s test
